context: Add encoding="utf-8" to both call sites. pyproject.toml is UTF-8 by spec (PEP 518) and TPC-DS query files are ASCII/UTF-8, so this is a correctness tightening with no behaviour change on Linux/macOS. Then consider extending the existing encoding lint/ratchet (see quality-bulk-fix-encoding-lint-and-ratchet, done) to forbid bare read_text()/open() in benchbox/ so the next one is caught at review time rather than in a nightly.
description: Supersedes product-read-text-missing-explicit-encoding-windows (dropped only to attach a work breakdown). Latent Windows defects in benchbox/, distinct from the test-side family. Path.read_text() with no encoding uses locale.getpreferredencoding(), which is cp1252 on Windows, so any non-ASCII byte raises UnicodeDecodeError ('charmap' codec can't decode byte ...). Two unguarded call sites: benchbox/utils/dependencies.py:37 reading pyproject.toml, and benchbox/core/tpcds_obt/query_conversion.py:161 reading a query file into self.raw_text. Found while triaging the Windows nightly; NOT currently covered by any failing test, which is why it is latent rather than red. Filed separately from windows-explicit-utf8-source-and-plan-fixtures because that item's only_modify is tests/** only and so cannot carry a benchbox/ fix; the charmap failure that IS red (test_cloud_storage_gate_deployment_aware.py:131) is test-side and belongs to that item.

preserves.behavior: Behaviour on Linux/macOS is unchanged; no new dependency on file locale

verifications.description: no bare read_text() remains in benchbox/
